newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Peronists dismiss tycoon's counter-attack.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Peronists dismiss tycoon's counter-attack.

text.p: Argentina's Peronist government on Thursday dismissed a legal counter-attack by tycoon and accused mobster Alfredo Yabran in the investigation into the January murder of a news photographer.
Yabran has been named by police as the only lead in the probe into who ordered the murder of photographer Jose Luis Cabezas in January.

The political overtones of the case, and Yabran's alleged friendship with President Carlos Menem, have kicked up a scandal that is a serious embarrassment to the ruling Peronists just ahead of key elections in Congress in October.
Yabran on Wednesday sued Buenos Aires Province Gov. Eduardo Duhalde for calling him a "suspect" in the case.
But Duhalde, a heavyweight in the ruling Peronist Party who is the main candidate to succeed President Carlos Menem in 1999, said at a news conference on Thursday that Yabran was not above the law.

"If he is a suspect, it is not because the press and this governor have plotted to sow doubts about him. Some powerful or important people think they deserve special treatment, but they are all equal before the law.
"I am not against Yabran, I am in favour of the truth...we don't need a scapegoat."
The murder of Cabezas, who was handcuffed, shot and burned, sparked mass public protests.

A former police officer has been arrested for the killing but police say the search for who ordered it leads to Yabran, who was reported to be annoyed by pictures taken by Cabezas for Noticias magazine. Although he has given evidence in the case, Yabran has not been charged.
Yabran has called himself "Public Enemy No.1" since former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo accused him of being the "head of the mafia" and laundering drug money.
Yabran, who admits to wealth of $400 million and a small stake in just one company, denies this and is suing Cavallo.

Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Justice Minister Elias Jassan have also been drawn into the centre of scandal after they were shown to have received calls from Yabran -- 100 calls in Jassan's case.
Yabran spokesman Wenceslao Bunge said Yabran would not make any comments outside his suit against Duhalde and against witnesses in the case who he has accused of faking evidence.

"We are enormously interested in the Cabezas case being solved because we know that we have nothing to do with it," Bunge told Reuters. "That is why we have decided to make no comments outside the court case."

But Secretary of the Fight Against Drug Addiction and Trafficking Julio Cesar Araoz said that since Yabran "made so much money from Argentine society...he shouldn't be afraid of showing how clean his businesses are."
